chapter_hint: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
page_hint: Ch 4 §6, Architecture Consequence, Economic feasibility bullet
quoted_clause: if the input token count could be reduced to 2 K (e.g. tighter retrieval/reranking to fewer chunks, context compression, or prefix caching), cost per request drops to ~$0.003
observed: Prefix caching is listed as a way to reduce the input token count. It does not reduce the number of input tokens; it reuses previously computed K/V for a shared prefix. It may reduce compute and, under some provider pricing schemes, reduce billed cost for cached tokens, but it is not a token-count reduction mechanism.
correction: Remove prefix caching from the parenthetical list of token-count reducers, or rewrite the sentence to distinguish “fewer input tokens (retrieval/reranking, context compression)” from “lower effective prefill cost for the same tokens (prefix caching, if the provider prices cached tokens favorably).”
acceptance_test: Verify that the revised passage does not claim prefix caching reduces input-token count and that any cost claim for prefix caching is explicitly tied to provider pricing or compute savings rather than token-count reduction.
verdict_evidence: chapter-04.md:251 lists prefix caching among 'reduced to 2 K' reducers; :249 calls it 'a distinct mechanism'; ch6:91 'compute-saving move ... not a latency knob'.
fix_instruction: Drop 'prefix caching' from the 2 K reducers; add 'or lower effective prefill cost (prefix caching, if priced favorably)'.

quoted_clause: FIGURE 4.1 (Six-dimension workload characterization mapped to architectural decisions)
observed: The caption's enumerated list of the six workload dimensions names the second dimension 'Traffic / concurrency', but the figure's corresponding box (row 2, left column) is labeled 'Request rate & arrival pattern'. The other five dimension names in the caption (Quality requirements, Token profile, Latency SLO, Economic constraints, Operational constraints) match the figure boxes verbatim, so this single mismatch is an inconsistency rather than an intentional synonym. A reader using the caption to locate a dimension in the figure will look for 'Traffic / concurrency' and not find that exact box. (Secondary, trivial: the caption's last decision term 'multi-region vs. single-region deployment' adds the word 'deployment' versus the figure box 'multi-region vs. single-region'.)
acceptance_test: After the edit, the six dimension names in the caption list must equal the six left-column box labels in the figure exactly; specifically the second item must read 'Request rate & arrival pattern' (or the box must be renamed to match the caption). Re-verify the remaining five pairs still match.
verdict_evidence: ch04:245 caption item 2 'Traffic / concurrency' vs box 'Request rate & arrival pattern' (fig_batch1.py:29); other five match verbatim; item 6 adds 'deployment'.
fix_instruction: Retitle box 2 or caption item 2 to one name, and drop 'deployment' from caption item 6.

quoted_clause: but the 140 GB footprint means KV cache for 9.2 K context adds ~20–30 GB of GPU memory per request at peak, leaving headroom but not abundance.
observed: The book computes this quantity precisely everywhere else (24.1 GB at 9.2K input-only, 24.9 GB at 9.5K resident) and uses the precise figure for the 17-slot screen, the 436 GB budget and the host counts. Here it degrades to a '~20–30 GB' range, and 'at peak' is undefined (peak of what — context length, concurrency, or traffic?). The reader cannot tell whether the range is a context-length sensitivity band or a rounding of 24.1 GB.
correction: Replace with the precise figure and name the basis: 'the 140 GB footprint means KV cache for 9.2K context adds ~24.1 GB of GPU memory per request (~24.9 GB on the resident slot-counting basis), leaving headroom but not abundance.' If a sensitivity band is intended, state the context range it corresponds to (e.g. '~24 GB at 9.2K, ~84 GB at 32K').
acceptance_test: Every per-request KV figure in Ch 4 is a single precise number with a named basis, or an explicitly parameterised range.
verdict_evidence: ch4:248 '~20–30 GB of GPU memory per request at peak'; next bullet (ch4:249) uses precise 24.1/24.9; same section two ways, 'at peak' undefined.
fix_instruction: Ch4:248 — replace '~20–30 GB ... at peak' with '~24.1 GB (24.9 GB on the resident slot-counting basis)'.

quoted_clause: At the canonical instance rate (~$20/hr per 8xH100 host), the canonical 6–21-host fleet on the owned/self-host basis is roughly **$87.6K–$306.6K/month** (6 hosts at ~$87.6K/month — $87,600 = 6 x 730 h default paid-occupancy input ~ $14.04/1K — up to 21 hosts always-on at peak, $306,600 ~ $49.13/1K (full-util 6/21; the provisioning-policy fleet is 9/32 — see the §8 parenthetical; and the 21-host rows are peak-provisioned capacity divided by the average 10 rps volume — a peak-capacity-cost-per-1K-average-volume figure, not a per-request cost at either traffic level: at the 40 rps peak volume of 24.96M/month (40 rps over the same active-hours window: 40 x 3,600 x 8 h x 260 workdays / 12), $306,600 / 24,960K ~ $12.28/1K)
observed: This paragraph re-derives, in parenthetical prose, the entire sidebar table that appears a few pages earlier in the same chapter: $87,600 / $14.04 per 1K, $306,600 / $49.13 per 1K, the 9/32 policy fleet, the 24.96M peak volume and the $12.28 per 1K figure. The mini-case's own contribution — the 50 rps growth scenario and its 26/37/39/40-host sizing — is buried between two blocks of repeated cost arithmetic. This is redundant repetition (class C): the second occurrence adds no new reasoning.
correction: Replace the parenthetical block with a one-line pointer: 'the canonical 6–21-host fleet costs $87.6K–$306.6K/month on the owned/self-host basis (~$14.04–$49.13 per 1K requests; see the §3 sidebar for the basis and the active-hours variant)'. Keep the mini-case's own new content — the 50 rps sizing, the prefill cross-check, and the distinction from the canonical 40 rps case.
acceptance_test: No number appears twice in Ch 4 unless the second occurrence adds a new derivation or a new basis; the mini-case's length is dominated by its own scenario, not by restated canonical costs.
verdict_evidence: ch4:273 restates $87,600/$14.04/$306,600/$49.13/9-32/24.96M/$12.28 already derived at ch4:85-95; mini-case's own 50 rps work sandwiched between repeats.
fix_instruction: Ch4:273 — collapse the cost parenthetical to a pointer to the section 3 sidebar (~$14.04-$49.13/1K) and keep the 50 rps content.
